Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

allow verb

also let, permit, be allowed, may I?, permission, let me see, may (be allowed), can (be allowed), could I …?, might I …?, give one’s consent, consent, may I leave?

classical

Ov. Pont. 1.3.36: immemorēs nōn sinit esse suī
Cic. Cat. 1.10: nōn feram, nōn patiar, nōn sinam (Lewis & Short)

sinō, sinere, sīvī, situm

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

let, allow

With an accusative and infinitive, or the subjunctive: sine sciam, let me know (Liv. 2.40.5, Lewis & Short). “Let me see” is sine videam, as Plautus has sine dīcam (Pers. 750) and sine pellegam (Ps. 61b); asking to be handed something to look at, he says cedo, ut īnspiciam (Curc. 654b).

Other words

  • licet, licēre, licuit (licitum est) — it is allowed; you may

    verb, impersonal, with the dative and an infinitive · classical · Cic. Off. 1.103: lūdō autem et jocō ūtī illō quidem licet; Plaut. Men. 158: Licet.; Traupman 28: licet, yes, OK, in answer to licetne mihi …?

    “Am I allowed to?” is licetne?, and the answer licet, “yes, you may; all right”.

  • permittō, permittere, permīsī, permissum — give leave, permit

    verb, third conjugation, with the dative · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.71.1: nisi ego eī permīsissem; Traupman 296; Traupman 339 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    With ut or an infinitive.

  • patior, patī, passus sum — let happen, put up with

    verb, third conjugation (-iō), deponent · also used · classical · Gell. 5.2.3: haud umquam īnscendī sēsē ab aliō nisi ab rēge passus sit; Cic. de Or. 1.126: nōn patiēbātur · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Often with a negative: nōn patiar, I won’t have it.

Examples

  • lūdō autem et jocō ūtī illō quidem licet, sed sīcut somnō et quiētibus cēterīs tum, cum gravibus sēriīsque rēbus satis fēcerimus

    we may enjoy play and jokes, but as we enjoy sleep and other rest: when we have done enough serious and weighty workCic. Off. 1.103

  • Concēde hūc ā foribus. — Fīat. — Etiam concēde hūc. — Licet.

    Come away from the door. — All right. — Further this way. — OK.Plaut. Men. 158

  • nesciō quā nātāle solum dulcēdine cūnctōs dūcit et immemorēs nōn sinit esse suī

    by some sweetness or other our native soil draws us all and does not let us forget itOv. Pont. 1.3.35–36

  • Sine pellegam. — Sinō, nam mihi videor cum eā fābulārier.

    Let me read it through. — Go on: it feels as if I were talking with her.Plaut. Ps. 61b–62

  • Licet (ut) videam.

    Let me see.Traupman 339

  • Licetne mihi abīre? — Licetne mihi (ut) abeam?

    May I leave?Traupman 344

See also let me go!, let.
